objective: Proofs and cited results: count = 2 L1 on box split bases (outline the cross-polytope, Golab pi 4), Q_d layers, trees and ladders (orders against growth), parity bases blank, the chain grid's reduction to an Ising law and its closed-form outline (strictly convex and analytic for every chain length), the weave's same-class isotropy (cited).
status: Proved 2026-11-18 (refereed R1, confirmed with fixes, no Block): on split bases the count is twice the number of separating splits (boxes: twice L1, Golab pi 4, k = lam = d; lam = 2 bases incl. NN's grids: twice L1 of the two orders); from the line's middle starts the ladder (k = 2) and the comb (k = 1) grow alike, so one start's growth does not read k (every start together tells them apart); parity bases blank; the state metric is blind to translation and, rooted at the all-equal state, determines k and lam; a chain of l not-all-equal knots with loose distinctions is the pair law (-1/3)^l; cited and checked: the chain grid's outline is strictly convex and analytic (no ellipse in any drawing), tending to the taxicab diamond, and the critical weave's is round (an ellipse in every drawing; a = 0.6322260823).
title: What is settled about count balls by construction and by classical results
